starting_state: A new empty project, stopped, with Record off. No channel has an output, no pattern has trigs and no masks are set. One MIDI output is available to choose on channel 1.

steps.caption: Starting point: a new, empty project, stopped, with Record off. No channel has an output, no pattern has trigs and no masks are set. Tap Channel (3,8): the header reads CH01. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, choose Device with E2 and press K3. Turn E3 one detent to the first output in the list and press K3 to apply it. Whichever name the row shows is fine for this walk-through; in your own project pick the note-capable output you set up in Connect a sound. The Device page for CH01 stays on screen.
Tap Pattern (5,8) for the Trig view of pattern 1, then tap steps (1,4), (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4). Four steps light on row 4. Each lit step is a trig, a moment where a note will sound.

Tap Channel (3,8), then tap pattern slot (1,2) to feed pattern 1 to channel 1. Next limit the channel to four steps: hold step 1 at (1,4), tap step 4 at (4,4), then release step 1. Hold the first step of the range, tap the last, then let go. The channel now loops steps 1 to 4, and those four steps are brighter than the rest of row 4.

Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll up to Masks with E2 and press K3. Select Note with E2, then turn E3 right until the screen reads C3, which is MIDI 60. The Note row shows the name, so stop on the readout instead of counting. With no step held this sets the channel note for all steps.
Turn E2 one detent to select Vel, then turn E3 right until the screen reads 80. Every step now plays at velocity 80, a medium-loud level.

Turn E2 one detent to select Len, then turn E3 until the screen reads 1/2, so each note lasts half a step. Tap Play (1,8) to hear four equal C notes (MIDI 60, velocity 80) repeating as the playhead runs along steps 1 to 4; the frame shows the Masks screen, so listen to your output or check the MIDI strip below. Tap Play again to stop.

provenance.scope: complete public playback validation, including two cycles, closing onset, releases and Stop

title: Create a four-step loop from an empty project
